item: W15 a bypass request from root outside a sandbox is refused

supportingModules.note: the environment probe class holding the sandbox exemption the guard consults: the platform test, the uid source, the IS_SANDBOX and CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP flags
the container marker itself: statSync("/.dockerenv") behind the probe class's isDocker()

coordinateUnit: zero-based UTF-16, left-closed/end-exclusive, over the decoded module text
readAs: inert data; no recovered entrypoint was executed

facts.name: the guard, and its refusal text
facts.symbol: function g(s){if(!i(s))return;if(jv.isRootOutsideDeliberateSandbox())console.error("--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons"),process.exit(1)}
facts.note: a process exit rather than a warning, and the message names the reason only

facts.name: the policy gate, not ported
facts.note: strips the mode and reports a policy-sourced notice

facts.name: the consent dialog and its persist check, not ported
facts.text: bypass consent was accepted but user settings do not show it (the write failed, or the file has an invalid value), so bypass is not passed on

facts.name: the three exports
facts.symbol: export{c as applyBypassPolicyGate,b as ensureAgentsBypassConsent,g as refuseBypassUnderRoot}

facts.name: the sandbox exemption
facts.note: root outside a deliberate sandbox: not Windows, uid 0, and neither sandbox flag set

facts.name: the two sandbox flags and the uid source

portedInvariant: A request for the permission mode that skips every check is refused before anything runs when the process is root outside a deliberate sandbox, because the tools would then act as the machine's owner rather than as the person who typed the command.

wiring.note: the call sits immediately after resolvePermissions, so the refusal precedes workspace locking, MCP admission, the task-required gate and the first request; the import is at src/cli.ts:15

implementation.localModeSpelling: the resolved mode is 'bypass' (src/permissions.ts:8), the local counterpart of the recovered 'bypassPermissions'

ownedDecisions: The decision is returned as a value and the CLI turns it into the exit, so the rule is observable by a test and explainable by a wrapper; the recovered function exits on its own.

Two sandbox signals rather than the recovered two flags: one environment opt-in (HARNESS_SANDBOX=1) plus the two container marker files, because being root under Docker or Podman is the intended arrangement here and there is no bubblewrap wrapper of our own to name.
Windows needs no platform test: process.getuid does not exist there, so the uid is undefined rather than 0 and nothing is refused.
A marker path that throws on stat counts as absent, so a permission error cannot be turned into an exemption.
The refusal names the reason and not a fix: which sandbox to use is the person's choice.
notPorted: applyBypassPolicyGate: this runtime's settings layers carry no policy source, and stripping the mode after resolving it would silently contradict the flag the person typed.
ensureAgentsBypassConsent: this runtime has no bypass consent dialog, so the rule guards a surface it does not have.

The settings-level spelling of the request (allowBypass === true): the local settings schema has no such field, so the mode is the only spelling that reaches the guard; an unreachable true branch in a security guard is left out deliberately.
The bubblewrap flag as such, covered by the container markers and the single opt-in.

added: only the mode that skips every check counts as a bypass request, over all five local modes plus empty and absent
root outside a container is refused and a non-root uid or an absent uid is not
each container marker and the literal opt-in value exempt, a non-literal value does not, and a marker that throws on stat does not
the refusal fires only for a bypass request made by root, and the real environment refuses nothing

the CLI refuses the mode before it starts anything: the child preloads process.getuid=()=>0 through a data: module, runs src/cli.ts with --permission-mode bypass, and asserts exit 1 with the message and no connection attempt, while --permission-mode plan under the same uid is not refused

cliSmoke.reason: the refusal is a pure function of the resolved mode and the process uid, and the real-CLI case above already drives the whole path end to end; a separate driver would repeat a passing check without reaching anything new.

regressions: None. The guard fires only for a mode no existing case uses together with a uid no test environment has, and both halves of that pair are needed before it refuses anything.
limitations: No real root session and no real container were used to confirm the exemption: the uid is injected, and the marker tests are the ones a Docker or Podman host would leave behind rather than files read from such a host.
The port is narrower than the recovered module: the policy gate and the consent dialog are not carried over, and the settings-level spelling of the request has no local producer.
The bubblewrap flag is not reproduced by name, so a bubblewrap sandbox that leaves neither marker file needs the explicit opt-in here.
